market_context: United States/general English; strained Greek yogurt versus plain regular yogurt
title: Greek yogurt vs. regular yogurt: protein, fat, and sugar

seo.title: Greek yogurt vs. regular yogurt: protein, fat, and sugar
seo.meta_description: Strained Greek yogurt can provide more than twice the protein of regular yogurt. Fat and sugar depend heavily on whether the product is whole, nonfat, or flavored.
seo.search_intent: Compare Greek and regular yogurt for protein, fat, sugar, calories, and serving size.

excerpt: Strained Greek yogurt usually contains much more protein than regular yogurt—often about 9–10 g versus 3.5–4.5 g per 100 g. Fat depends on whether either product is whole, low-fat, or nonfat, and the 4–5 g of sugar in plain yogurt is mostly naturally occurring lactose. Flavored versions can contain far more added sugar.
content_html:
Greek yogurt's biggest nutritional advantage is not mysterious: straining removes part of the whey and water, concentrating the milk solids that remain. That is why a true strained Greek yogurt can contain more than twice as much protein per 100 g as conventional yogurt.

Fat and sugar are less predictable because either style can be sold whole, low-fat, nonfat, plain, or sweetened.

Straining is what creates the protein gap

A representative comparison between plain whole-milk products looks like this:

Per 100 gPlain Greek yogurtPlain regular yogurt
Protein~9–10 g~3.5–4.5 g
Fat~4–5 g~3–4 g
Naturally occurring sugars~3–4.5 g~4–5 g
Calories~90–100 kcal~60–70 kcal

The protein did not appear during processing. Removing whey and water simply leaves more protein in the same 100 g of finished yogurt.

Fat depends more on the version than the word Greek

Nonfat Greek yogurt may provide around 9–10 g protein with almost no fat. Whole Greek yogurt can contain 4–5 g fat per 100 g or more. Regular yogurt can also be nonfat or whole.

That means “Greek” does not automatically mean high-fat and “regular” does not automatically mean low-fat. The milk-fat percentage on the label matters more.

Plain yogurt contains sugar even when none is added

Milk naturally contains lactose. A plain unsweetened yogurt commonly shows around 4–5 g sugar per 100 g even if the ingredient list contains no added sugar.

Flavored yogurts are a different comparison. Fruit preparations, cane sugar, syrups, or other sweeteners can push total sugar to 10–15 g per 100 g or more. That difference can dwarf the small natural-sugar gap between plain Greek and plain regular yogurt.

A single serving makes the protein difference meaningful

A 6-ounce serving, about 170 g, of Greek yogurt with 9 g protein per 100 g provides about 15 g protein. The same amount of regular yogurt at 4 g per 100 g provides roughly 7 g.

An 8 g difference in one snack or breakfast is large enough to matter if protein intake is the reason you are choosing yogurt in the first place.

What about calcium?

Straining removes some whey, so Greek yogurt does not necessarily concentrate calcium to the same degree as protein. Regular yogurt can provide as much or more calcium per 100 g depending on the product.

If calcium is the priority, check the label rather than assuming the thicker yogurt contains more of every nutrient.

Which one is better?

For more protein per serving, strained Greek yogurt usually wins clearly. For fewer calories, a plain regular yogurt may be lower if you are comparing whole-milk versions, although nonfat Greek yogurt can combine high protein with very few calories.

The practical rule is to compare protein, fat, and added sugar on the label. The style name tells you something about texture and processing, but the nutrition panel tells you whether the product actually fits your goal.

faq.question: Does Greek yogurt have more protein than regular yogurt?
faq.answer: Usually yes if it is strained: roughly 9–10 g protein per 100 g versus around 3.5–4.5 g in regular yogurt.

faq.question: Is Greek yogurt higher in fat?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Greek yogurt can be nonfat, low-fat, or whole. Compare the specific products rather than the style name alone.

faq.question: Why does plain yogurt contain sugar if no sugar is added?
faq.answer: Milk naturally contains lactose, so plain unsweetened yogurt usually contains several grams of naturally occurring sugar.
